grand_strategy.reading:
Spain's grand strategy is the strategy of a middle power that has chosen to be
ruled by its law and its domestic coalition rather than by its geography, and
geography is now collecting. Madrid's south is a border with a monarchy it
cannot afford to quarrel with and a gas pipeline from a republic that cannot
be ignored; its east is an energy island; its west an ally; its north a
grudging partner (France) and a flat refusal of the Atlantic bill (2.1%
against 5%). The Sanchez government answered each pressure with a legal
gesture (the Sahara letter of 2022, Palestine in 2024, the arms embargo of
2025, the bases refusal of 2026, regularisation), which won votes and
moral standing but accumulated debts: Trump now names Spain as the outlier,
Israel and Spain have downgraded embassies, Morocco reopened Ceuta and
Melilla in August 2026 after a mass crossing, Italy suspended Schengen
arrangements for a month. The Luttwak reading is that the gestures were
cheap while the system was friendly, and became expensive when friction
arrived in a pile - Iran war, Ceuta, NATO summit, Trump, an election. Two
signals that are not rows: the government itself justifies the 2.1% line by the welfare
state and public finances, so it is a domestic bargain as much as a
strategy, and the snap election of 29 Nov 2026 makes every position here
provisional: polls point to a PP-led government with Vox, whose foreign
line on Gaza, Iran and Latin America would likely differ.
